articles.title: Isaac Brown brings Louisville back from the brink as Cardinals pummel Florida State 44-20
articles.summary: (AP) — Isaac Brown ran for a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on just 17 carries, including a game-changing 97-yard score, as Louisville rallied to t...
articles.body:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — Isaac Brown ran for a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on just 17 carries, including a game-changing 97-yard score, as Louisville rallied to take down Florida State 44-20 on Friday night.

Known for his big-play capabilities, Brown's long touchdown run came on the first play of a second-quarter drive after Louisville DB Kaleb Beasley stopped Florida State WR Jasen Lopez at the Cardinals 3 on a fourth-and-goal. The Seminoles had led 14-0 and appeared to be in total control of the game.

After the game, Florida State coach Mike Norvell said he still felt good about the play, a screen pass from Ashton Daniels to Lopez, with the possibility of going up by three touchdowns on the road.

"Unfortunately, we didn't do a good enough job in that moment," said Norvell, whose team lost its 11th straight road game. "They're pinned back. They got to go 98 yards, and they did it in one play."

The touchdown run set a record for Louisville's longest play from scrimmage, and Brown's total for the night was the most for any running back among Football Bowl Subdivision programs this season.

Louisville (3-3, 2-2 Atlantic Coast Conference) outgained the Seminoles 438-190 after the fourth-down stop. The Cardinals finished with 537 yards. That included 397 overall on the ground, where they accounted for all of their touchdowns. It also happened despite Keyjuan Brown, the Cardinals' top rusher this season, being sidelined with an injury.

"Just when you think things are looking as bleak as they can, our guys hung in there," said Louisville coach Jeff Brohm, whose team snapped a two-game skid. "You got to give our guys a ton of credit for playing hard, for finishing the game, for sticking together, for believing in themselves and their teammates. That's not easy to do.'

Brown started the second half taking the opening kickoff 71 yards to the Seminoles 28 and got a horse-collar penalty added at the end. Four plays later, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz scored on a 3-yard run, his first of two scores, to give the Cardinals a 21-14 lead.

He then finished his night with a 68-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter.

Daniels completed 21 of 37 passes for 209 yards and two touchdowns as Florida State (3-3, 1-2) amassed 362 yards on offense. He also ran for a score.

Florida State: There has been a lot of head scratching about the Seminoles' football program in recent years. Another questionable decision came when they chose not to kick a short field goal early in the second quarter to potentially take a 17-0 lead over Louisville. But the Cardinals made it a moot point by scoring the next 35 points.

Louisville: There will be a lot of talk about Brown, but give the Cardinals defense credit. They started out slow, but after Brown's big run, they shut down the Seminoles in a game Louisville really needed to win.

Three kneeldowns to end the game kept the Cardinals from registering their ninth 400-yard rushing game in program history. As it was, the 397 was the most a Louisville team racked up since getting 411 against Syracuse on Nov. 11, 2018.

Florida State, meanwhile, had its worst rushing defense game since Georgia Tech amassed 401 yards on Oct. 10, 2009.

Florida State departed Louisville after the loss. However, rather than head straight home to Tallahassee, the team chartered a flight to Jacksonville to avoid flying into Hurricane Isaias. The hurricane made landfall near Destin, Fla., located about 150 miles west of the Florida state capital, earlier Friday evening.

From Jacksonville, the team would bus back to campus, which a team spokesperson said would add a couple hours to the trip.

Florida State plays at No. 4 Miami on Oct. 17.

Louisville plays at Syracuse on Oct. 17.

articles.title: Hay que entender que al fútbol se juega con la cabeza, no con los pies
articles.standfirst: 'Comprimidos', por Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.summary: 'Comprimidos', por Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.body: He asistido esta semana a un encuentro organizado por un ‘Think Tank’ vinculado al Benfica llamado Unum. Allí conocí a un legendario futbolista del club lisboeta: Antonio Simoes. Camino de cumplir 83 años, posee el récord de ser el jugador más joven en ganar una Copa de Europa. Lo logró, ante el Real Madrid en 1962, cuando tenía 18 años y 139 días. Lúcido, inteligente y reflexivo, con la sapiencia que dan la gloria y la experiencia, comer y cenar a su lado fue como asistir a una impagable lección magistral de fútbol. § “Para triunfar en el fútbol lo primero que hay que entender es que se juega con la cabeza, no con los pies”. En esta sentencia de Simoes estriba la diferencia entre jugadores. Se podría añadir, con rabiosa actualidad, que no sólo hay que usar la cabeza dentro del terreno de juego: hay que hacerlo también fuera del césped. Y si el futbolista (no doy nombres, no creo que sea necesario) no es capaz de entender esto tan sencillo, para eso están (o deberían estar) quienes les asesoran. § “Yo no tuve muchos entrenadores porque éramos muy buenos”. Certero y atinado Simoes. Una frase para pensar. § La España coral de De la Fuente parece un equipo delicado que, sin embargo, tumba a los rivales a martillazos. § Convendría no subestimar a la UEFA en el ‘caso Negreira’. § Tras el largo y desacostumbrado parón de selecciones vuelve LaLiga. Hay ganas. § La posibilidad de ver jugar en un mismo equipo a Cristiano Ronaldo y a Leo Messi, que está intentando impulsar Carlos Tévez, ya la movimos desde MARCA hace tiempo, pero era cuando ambos estaban en el momento cumbre de sus carreras y, aunque fue bien acogida, no encontró el momento oportuno. § Comparto una bonita frase que le he escuchado a Sergio Camello, un futbolista que, por cierto, merecería más galones y reconocimiento: “El Rayo Vallecano es el último equipo que queda del fútbol de otra época”. § Más de mil deportistas compiten este fin de semana en la primera edición de Hyatlón, que se celebra en el Polideportivo Gallur de Madrid. Una modalidad deportiva que avanza sin freno hacia los Juegos Olímpicos. § El ‘fichaje’ de Shai Gilgeous-Alexander por el Atlético de Madrid vuelve a demostrar lo que digo siempre, que el fútbol tiene un guion tan infinito como imprevisible. § Esta página no está patrocinada por Sancor Seguros.

articles.title: Mike Norvell's FSU Contract Buyout, Details Revealed Amid Hot Seat Buzz After Loss to Louisville
articles.summary: Florida State could be one step closer to considering one of the largest coaching contract buyouts in college football history after Friday night's 44-20 loss to Louisville.
articles.body:
Florida State could be one step closer to considering one of the largest coaching contract buyouts in college football history after Friday night's 44-20 loss to Louisville.

The Seminoles fell to 3-3 on the season, and 10-20 in their last three seasons under head coach Mike Norvell, following the blowout loss.

Responding by moving on from Norvell, who is under contract with Florida State through 2031, would be a costly proposition for FSU.

Norvell's contract states he will receive 85 percent of his salary in addition to supplemental funding in case of a buyout, per USA Today's Dan Rorabaugh .

That buyout total was a projected $47.7 million as of Oct. 3, the same day Norvell made his case to stay in his position by leading his team to a win over Virginia, per Rorabaugh.

Norvell's projected buyout would drop to about $46.5 million by Dec. 1, Rorabaugh reported.

Only four coaches have been fired with buyouts worth more than $45 million, including Virginia Tech coach James Franklin, who was fired by Penn State in October 2025.

Like Penn State's buyout of Franklin, Rorabaugh noted the ultimate cost of a potential FSU buyout would be mitigated if Norvell is hired elsewhere.

The cost of parting ways with Norvell could be more expensive than just buying out his contract. On3's Pete Nakos reported the cost of firing Norvell's staff in addition to hiring a replacement is projected to be around $100 million.

Florida State is now riding an 11-game road losing streak into next weekend, during which the Seminoles are slated to take on their highest-ranked opponent of the season so far on Saturday at No. 4 Miami.

articles.title: Sampdoria, Bordeaux, Real Zaragoza: Ranking European football's biggest sleeping giants
articles.summary: From Sampdoria to Saint-Etienne and Real Zaragoza, who are the sleeping giants of European football?
articles.body:
Deportivo, Parma, Hamburg. Not just a football hipster's holiday hit-list, but a sample of erstwhile headline acts who have returned to their respective top flights in recent years.

You can throw Leeds United, Nottingham Forest, Schalke and Malaga into the mix too.

But with such footballing royalty back in the big time, where can you find Europe's current sleeping giants? Which one-mighty sides are still snoozing?

We first need to establish some criteria - history, heritage, fanbase, stadium. Clubs with huge potential who currently exist outside the top flight.

Calling a big city home helps, but it is not a deal-maker - sorry to fans of Bristol City and second-tier Russian outfit FC Ufa, where the local population tops one million.

Likewise, some clubs with good-sized stadiums have not made the cut. Bari, whose Stadio San Nicola is the third-largest in Italy and was built for Italia '90, stands out, though some of their calcio colleagues outside Serie A also have grounds of more than 30,000 - Hellas Verona, Messina and Palermo among them.

There's a plethora of ex-Premier League teams with top-flight worthy arenas and storied pasts, while Germany is stacked full of historic clubs with huge homes who arguably deserve a spot - Fortuna Dusseldorf, Wolfsburg, Hannover 96 - but we can't include them all.

A sleeping giant must have experienced some element of former glory and Pro Vercelli are the obvious candidate there, winning seven Italian titles by 1922. But, despite being under new ownership, the third-tier side boast neither the ground nor local population to awaken that historic status any time soon.

The other nuance is, that success cannot have come too recently. West Ham, for example, won a European competition three years ago, Wolves are recent top-flight regulars; likewise Stade de Reims, twice European Cup runners-up, and eight-time French champions Nantes.

Leaving out Steaua Bucharest was another big call. European Cup winners 40 years ago and Romania's most dominant club, they now play in Liga II. But, following a deeply divisive split, many of the traditional fanbase follow top-flight FCSB. So who really owns that legacy?

And there was a case for Boavista, title winners in 2001 but whose existence now hangs by a thread. Facing financial ruin, despite fans' best efforts, they have been ejected from Portugal's professional leagues.

Anyway, let's get on with this. Piped through the matrix above, here are my top 10 European sleeping giants - you can have your say in the comments, too.

League titles: One (2009-10). Domestic cups: One (1985-86). Division: 1.Lig, second tier. Stadium: Centennial Ataturk Stadium (43,361)

Historically dominated by Istanbul's elite teams, Bursaspor snapped that long-running streak by becoming only the second club from outside of the capital - and first since Trabzonspor almost three decades earlier - to clinch the Turkish title in 2010.

That meant Champions League nights against Manchester United and Rangers, but in 2024 the Green Crocodiles dropped into the fourth tier for the first time in their history.

Based in a city of about 2.5m people - Bursa sits in the north west, south of Istanbul, near Mount Uludag - and with a unique crocodile-shaped stadium that can house 43,361 fans, Bursaspor have soared up the pyramid since and are looking to return to the Super Lig for the first time since 2019.

League titles: Eight (most recent East German DDR-Oberliga 1989-90). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 89-90). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion (32,085).

Without wanting to turn this into a 2.Bundesliga table, this is the first of four German entries. But Dynamo Dresden, bearing a complex history and situated in the underrepresented east, feel a little different.

Initially enjoying the support of the security forces before their best players were relocated to Berlin, Dynamo became European regulars and lost to Liverpool in the Uefa Cup in 1976 and European Cup two seasons later.

One of East Germany's most dominant clubs, they won eight titles and seven cups and joined the Bundesliga in 1991 following reunification, but they dropped into the third tier four years later amid relegation and mounting debts.

Dynamo, with alumni including Matthias Sammer, have bounced around the regional and lower leagues for many years but now sit in 2.Bundesliga.

Based in a city of more than half a million people, their potential is underpinned by a large, passionate fanbase who averaged over 30,000 for home games in the second tier last term.

League titles: Four (most recent 1997-98). Domestic cups: Two (most recent 95-96). Division: 2.Bundesliga. Stadium: Fritz-Walter-Stadion (49,327)

With their 1997-98 success, Kaiserslautern remain the only side to win the Bundesliga immediately after promotion, albeit following a surprise relegation having also been champions in 1991 and enjoyed cup triumphs in 1990 and 1996.

European regulars in the 1990s and early 2000s, it is now almost 15 years since they competed in the Bundesliga, spending four seasons in the third tier before a promotion in 2022.

Despite modest league finishes, the club continue to record average crowds of more than 46,000 and almost pulled off another shock in 2024 when they reached the German Cup final, losing to Xabi Alonso's Leverkusen.

League titles: Four (most recent 1929-30). Domestic cups: Four (most recent 90-91). Division: League One, third tier. Stadium: Hillsborough (39,732)

Sheffield United fans may argue that they, not city rivals Sheffield Wednesday, should make this list. But the Owls edge it on history and heritage - even if the most recent of their four league titles came almost 100 years ago.

Wednesday were League Cup winners in 1991, and in living memory for many gave us magical moments from the likes of David Hirst, Chris Waddle and Paolo di Canio. Yet they now sit in the third tier after entering administration and enduring relegation last season, before a US consortium bought the club in May.

The Owls, boasting England's 12th biggest club stadium, were relegated from the top flight in 2000, but fans are fuelled with fresh optimism that a reawakening is possible.

Leagues: Two (most recent 1931). Domestic cups: Two (most recent 2002). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Olympiastadion (74,475).

I'm convinced Hertha have huge potential, if not the history to match some of their counterparts. Their only titles, for example, precede the Bundesliga era.

But the Old Lady once reached a Uefa Cup semi-final and beat Chelsea in the Champions League in 1999.

This season is their fourth consecutive campaign outside the top tier, but Hertha continue to play at Berlin's Olympiastadion and regularly attract more than 50,000 fans. A new ground on the Olympic Park site, housing up to 52,000, is being considered.

Currently top of 2.Bundesliga, Hertha can tap into a deep talent pool on their doorstep - highly rated youngsters Ibrahim Maza and Kennet Eichhorn have joined Leverkusen, goalkeeper Tjark Ernst went to Feyenoord - and look equipped to return to the Bundesliga in fine shape.

Leagues: Six (most recent 2008-09). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 12-13). Division: Regional 1, sixth tier. Stadium: Stade Atlantique (42,115)

Bordeaux's recent troubles have been well documented. Relegated from Ligue 1 in 2022 before administration meant they tumbled into the fourth tier, this summer they were again demoted to the regional sixth tier because of financial issues.

Having seemingly hit the bottom, the 2009 French champions now at least have something to build on after being bought by US investment fund Park Bench for one euro.

Les Girondins are dripping in history. Once home to former greats Jean Tigana and Zinedine Zidane, as well as current France internationals Aurelien Tchouameni and Jules Kounde, their decade-old home hosted a Euro 2016 quarter-final - albeit Bordeaux are not playing there at present as they try to shape their future.

League titles: Nine (most recent 1967-68). Domestic cups: Four (most recent 06-07). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Max-Morlock-Stadion (50,000).

Perhaps it's not overly imaginative to be opting for the current top two in Germany's second tier but FC Nuremberg meet all the selection criteria laid out above.

They have the history - nine titles, with the latest of four cup triumphs coming in 2007; a 50,000-seater home; large local fanbase in a one-club city - and the heritage.

They're nicknamed 'Der Club' because of their status in early German football.

Oh, and World Cup winner and Germany's all-time top goalscorer Miroslav Klose is their boss.

Domestic cups: Six (most recent 2003-04). European: Cup Winners' Cup (1994-95). Division: Primera Federacion, third tier. Stadium: La Romareda (under reconstruction but projected 43,000).

David Seaman, look away now. Arsenal fans of a certain vintage will remember former Spurs boy Nayim's long, looping winner beating the moustachioed stopper in the final minute of extra time to give Real Zaragoza the Cup Winners' Cup.

There have been two Copa del Rey triumphs, European journeys and star names since - Pablo Aimar, Diego Milito and David Villa among them - but three decades later, Los Manos find themselves in Spain's third tier.

Ander Herrera, aged 37, is back at his boyhood club , who are in the process of developing a new 43,114-capacity stadium for the 2030 World Cup, in an attempt to help the fallen giants return to former glories.

"Real Zaragoza belong to Europe, they belong to compete for trophies, to be fighting with the biggest clubs in Spain and in Europe," said Herrera.

League titles: 10 (most recent 1980–81). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 2012–13). Continental: European Cup runners-up (1975–76). Division: Ligue 2, second division. Stadium: Stade Geoffroy-Guichard (41,965)

Saint-Etienne were, until Paris St-Germain overtook them in the past decade, the most-decorated club in France with 10 league titles in 25 seasons from 1956-57 to 1980-81.

Les Verts reached the European Cup final in 1976, losing to a vintage Bayern Munich side, while their last silverware came in the now-defunct Coupe de la Ligue 13 years ago with a team spearheaded by Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

They are presently spending their fourth season in five in the second tier, but they continue to produce top prospects. Star defenders William Saliba and Wesley Fofana came off the production line, while 18-year-old attacking talent Djylian N'Guessan will join Liverpool in January.

Then there is their 41,965-capacity Stade Geoffroy-Guichard home, nicknamed the 'cauldron', which was a whisker from seeing Ligue 1 football again this term - Les Verts lost to Nice in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning the wait to rejoin France's elite continues.

League titles: 1990-91. Domestic cups: Four (most recent 93–94). Continental: Cup Winners' Cup (89–90), European Cup runners-up (91-92). Division: Serie B, second tier. Stadium: Stadio Luigi Ferraris (33,205)

Sampdoria were once continental big-hitters, not merely domestic champions during a golden era of Italian football.

Buoyed by Paolo Mantovani's investment, the Genoa outfit won the Coppa Italia four times between 1985 and 1994, clinched the Scudetto in 1991 and reached three European finals, winning the Cup Winners' Cup in 1990 a year after losing to Barcelona in the final.

In 1992, the team of Gianluca Vialli, Roberto Mancini and Gianluca Pagliuca were again beaten by Barcelona in extra time of the European Cup final at Wembley.

More big names followed in the period between Sven-Goran Eriksson's side winning the club's last major trophy in 1994 and a first relegation five years later - Clarence Seedorf, Juan Sebastian Veron and Ariel Ortega included.

Samp had spells back in Europe before finishing bottom of Serie A in 2023 amid serious financial problems and almost dropped into the third tier.

Under new ownership, though, fans hope the club's future is more stable - and the architecturally iconic Stadio Luigi Ferraris home they share with rivals Genoa is set to undergo an expensive redevelopment before Italy host Euro 2032.

articles.title: Man Utd stalwart set for double role as Carrick confirms two international break injuries
articles.summary: Diogo Dalot will have a key role to play in the coming weeks, as Manchester United’s full-back department has been pared down to the bone.After a torrid star...
articles.body:
Diogo Dalot will have a key role to play in the coming weeks, as Manchester United's full-back department has been pared down to the bone.

After a torrid start to the season, the Premier League giants cannot afford another misstep, especially when they host fellow strugglers Tottenham Hotspur.

The two sides will lock horns at Old Trafford on Saturday afternoon (17:30 UK time), but the Red Devils will have to negotiate this contest and the following ones with limited options.

Michael Carrick confirms Dorgu, Mazraoui & Sesko Absences

(Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

On Friday, Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick offered mixed injury updates. He revealed that Carlos Baleba, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, and Amad Diallo are all making important strides in their recovery.

However, he confirmed that Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui have picked up injuries during the international break , which will rule them out of action, while Benjamin Sesko could be set for another long spell on the treatment table due to an injury relapse.

"Patrick came off and looks like he'll be out for a number of weeks. Nouss came off and took a knock. He's not quite right, so we'll see how he is," said the 45-year-old in his pre-match press conference via the Manchester Evening News .

"Carlos is improving, has trained a lot, Amad, Kobbie and Marcus have done a little bit of training. Ben is further away with the injury he has, so he won't be ready."

Why Diogo Dalot will be key going forward

With Mazraoui unavailable, Dalot is the only natural first-team option left for Man Utd for the right-back role.

Moreover, the lack of available left-backs could see Dalot moved to the opposite side of the pitch, with Leny Yoro fielded at right-back (he was already tested in that role during pre-season).

Luke Shaw remains United's ultimate option at left-back, but his physical condition has been shaky this season, and many doubt his ability to play twice per week.

Sadly for Carrick, he won't be able to count on Dorgu or Mazraoui to rotate with the experienced Englishman, so switching Dalot to the left side could be his best solution.

Unlike Shaw, Dalot should be able to cope with the packed schedule, and although some of his recent MUFC displays weren't too convincing, he's coming off a positive international break, helping Portugal maintain a perfect record in the UEFA Nations League after winning all of their four fixtures.

The Braga native enjoyed back-to-back influential cameos. Against Denmark, he provided the assist to Joao Felix to secure a 4-2 victory. His second-half introduction versus Norway also paid dividends, as he was involved in the play that culminated in Goncalo Ramos' winner.

Against Erling Haaland and Co, Dalot recorded a passing accuracy of 92.3%, won all of his ground duels and recorded a top speed of 32.6 km/h, thus adding energy, intensity and quality to Portugal's play.

Man Utd fans will be hoping to witness this inspiring version of the Porto academy product at Old Trafford.

articles.title: Chelsea Star’s Injury Nightmare Is Finally Over
articles.summary: Revealed at Saint-Étienne at a young age and praised for his maturity and defensive qualities, Wesley Fofana quickly became one of the most promising center...
articles.body:
Revealed at Saint-Étienne at a young age and praised for his maturity and defensive qualities, Wesley Fofana quickly became one of the most promising center backs of his generation.

After a short season with the professionals in the Forez region, Fofana joined England and signed with Leicester. His impressive spell with the Foxes in the Premier League confirmed his immense potential, convincing Chelsea to spend slightly more than 80 million euros in the summer of 2022 to make him the pillar of its defensive line in the years to come.

However, the French defender's London trajectory has not been the one expected so far. After accumulating physical setbacks and a serious cruciate ligament rupture, Fofana has missed 124 matches in the Blues shirt since his arrival and has failed to live up to the enormous expectations placed on him.

Each return to the field offered glimpses of his anticipation and aggression, but too many physical uncertainties kept his consistency at the highest level compromised for a long time.

Wesley Fofana's Chelsea Turnaround Revealed After 124 Matches Missed

Now 25, the Marseille native finally seems to have exorcised his demons and found the consistency he lacked. After a 38-match season last year, he appears physically liberated and injury-free at the start of this season.

From there, Fofana strings together starts and rediscovers the explosiveness, aerial dominance, and duel-winning sharpness that made him one of the English league's most feared defenders.

Within Xabi Alonso's tactical setup at Chelsea, whether in a back three or a back four, the Frenchman has become a true cornerstone in the eyes of the Spanish coach. Alongside Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill or Josh Acheampong, Fofana has become undroppable.

Before the latter's arrival, Fofana had in fact praised the confidence Alonso could give to the Stamford Bridge squad: "I think everyone knows we need stability. We talked about it last season with the directors, and they said the same thing. Of course, we need results […], but we need stability, and I think he [Xabi Alonso] is the right person for that."

His ability to play out cleanly under pressure and his authority inevitably appeal to Alonso, who returns that trust. Solid, serene, and back at the top of his game, Fofana is finally proving his talent and establishing himself as one of the strong men in the London project this season. A reality he had always known, regardless of his past coaches at Chelsea, who always named him an undroppable starter.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso Issues Blunt Chelsea Warning After Slow Start
articles.summary: Chelsea started the Xabi Alonso era perfectly, with two wins in the first two Premier League matchdays and a style of play that quickly generated enthusiasm....
articles.body:
Chelsea started the Xabi Alonso era perfectly, with two wins in the first two Premier League matchdays and a style of play that quickly generated enthusiasm.

But a few weeks later, the momentum stalled. After losing to Arsenal (2-1), drawing with Hull City (2-2), and being heavily beaten by Brentford (3-0), the Blues now sit 10th with 7 points, having conceded 12 goals in five matchdays, or 2.4 goals per match.

The problem is all the more concerning because Chelsea also conceded three goals to Leeds in the League Cup, and its 3-4-2-1 system is struggling to offer enough defensive guarantees for now.

Alonso himself acknowledged it after Brentford: "We lost consistency over the course of the match, in the competitor's mentality, which was necessary in the second half." The Spaniard also insisted on the corrections to be made: "It's a set of things to review. We have to work on the mentality, the play, the tactics. We must continue to progress."

However, it's premature to talk about a deep crisis at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea remains a project under construction and still has impressive attacking arguments.

Cole Palmer, who missed the international break, has rediscovered his efficiency with four goals and three assists, while Morgan Rogers quickly established himself with three goals and four assists.

João Pedro is also one of the season's biggest surprises, with six goals and four assists in five starts, even though his presence against Bournemouth remains very uncertain.

A fresh Palmer return could be valuable, while Estevão, also decisive for Brazil during the break, offers an interesting alternative. But Chelsea must now find a better balance between that attacking force and a worrying defense: Maxence Lacroix is making encouraging individual debuts, but the collective concedes far too many chances and goals.

Xabi Alonso Issues Blunt Chelsea Warning After Slow Start: 'We Need Time'

Alonso was already asking for time after the first five matchdays: "It's a process. We have only played five matches in a very competitive Premier League. (…) We need time."

The schedule will allow us to measure Chelsea's ability to react. The Blues will host Bournemouth this Saturday before traveling to Everton, then hosting Tottenham and Manchester United in the league.

Meanwhile, Liverpool will also stand in their way in the League Cup. In other words, this match against Bournemouth is already an important appointment to restart the machine. Chelsea cannot afford to drop more points if it truly wants to return to the race for European places and, eventually, move closer to the teams capable of challenging for the title.

The season is still long, but after a 10th-place finish last season and the absence of European competition, expectations are inevitably high.

One key will also be Xabi Alonso's ability to evolve his attacking setup. His 3-4-2-1 uses three center backs, two wing-backs, and a highly mobile attacking line, with Malo Gusto notably able to come inside and Pedro Neto used in a role that doesn't match a natural full-back.

On the left, the competition between Chavarría, Palestra, and other options is not yet fully settled. This system offers many attacking options, but it also exposes Chelsea when the block loses control. Against Brentford, the Blues once again paid for their lack of consistency, and Levi Colwill himself acknowledged that the team still had to adapt to the new demands, particularly on set pieces.

This fragility is all the more surprising because Chelsea invested considerably to accompany Alonso's arrival. Chelsea spent more than 400 million euros during the transfer window, with Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Dibu Martinez, Palestra, and several other reinforcements intended to strengthen a squad that must aim much higher.

But the arrivals also bring delicate situations, like Estevão, who had already been reported as worried about his limited playing time under Alonso. The Brazilian, however, used the break to show his qualities for the national team, which could give the Spanish coach an additional option if João Pedro misses the Bournemouth match.

Chelsea must therefore find the right combination now, without calling its entire project into question at the first sign of a downturn. Because above all, it is important to remain measured: Chelsea is not the only team struggling.

Manchester United is also in a complicated period, Aston Villa is very low, and Tottenham is currently at the bottom, proving the Premier League remains particularly unpredictable. But with the Blues' ambitions and the resources available to Alonso, 10th place won't last.

articles.title: Former Manchester United player implores club to push for Harry Kane
articles.summary: FC Bayern is not selling Harry Kane to Manchester United.
articles.body:
Quinton Fortune knows a thing or two about Manchester United. The former South African international spent seven seasons at Old Trafford from 1999 to 2006, making more than 100 appearances for the club and winning three Premier League titles, a Champions League, and an FA Cup.

Now, Fortune is making a very simple argument about what his former club should do if it gets the opportunity to sign Harry Kane. According to Fortune, United should not hesitate.

"He's not young but given what he's achieved, Man Utd should go and get Harry Kane as soon as possible, whatever it takes. He is exactly what they need," Fortune told BOYLE Sports, who offers the latest Premier League odds . "If there's any chance of bringing Harry Kane in, do whatever it takes because the man is a natural-born goalscorer. Give him service and he will score goals. It's as simple as that. You give him service, he will put the ball in the back of the net. Just go and get him. Simple as that. If there's a possibility, there's a small chance of going to it. Don't wait any longer because what a player he is, my goodness."

It is difficult to get much more emphatic than that, but the reality is that Kane is not going anywhere.

Fortune's argument is built around something that has defined Kane throughout his career — goals. The England captain has consistently demonstrated that he does not need to dominate a match to decide it. Give him the right service, and he can turn opportunities into goals. That is also why the idea of Kane returning to England would generate so much interest.

Kane has already rewritten plenty of records since moving to Bayern Munich, while continuing to produce at an extraordinary level. He has shown that his game is about far more than simply finishing chances, too. His ability to link play, bring teammates into attacks, create opportunities, and still operate as an elite finisher makes him an unusual profile for a striker.

Fortune clearly believes that is exactly what United needs. However, Kane remains under contract with Bayern Munich and is rumored to be closing in on a two-year extension with the Englishman. So while Fortune may be dreaming of Kane in Manchester, FC Bayern supporters know that the answer to United's hypothetical pursuit remains a very simple one — better luck next time.

articles.title: Michel Sanchez Provides Injury Update On Ajax Left-Back Caio Henrique
articles.summary: Michel Sanchez has provided an injury update on Caio Henrique ahead of Ajax's game against NEC Nijmegen.
articles.body:
Will Ajax win the Eredivisie this season?

During the summer transfer window, Ajax completed the signing of Caio Henrique from AS Monaco in a transfer worth a reported fee of around €10 million, with various reports claiming that the fee could rise to €14 million through bonuses.

The Brazilian signed a four-year contract with Ajax, keeping him at the Johan Cruijff ArenA until June 2030.

Henrique has made 12 appearances for Ajax in all competitions so far and has started six of the club's seven Eredivisie matches this season.

Against Excelsior, however, Henrique was forced off after 23 minutes due to an injury. Owen Wijndal replaced him and played left-back for the rest of the game, which ended in a 2-2 draw.

In his press conference before Ajax's game against NEC Nijmegen on Saturday night in Amsterdam, Michel Sanchez provided an update on Henrique's current fitness following his injury.

"He is injured and will not be playing for the next few weeks," Michel said, speaking on Henrique's injury.

"He is mainly suffering from a thigh injury. The medical staff needs to investigate this further."

Henrique was not the only left-back Ajax signed during the summer transfer window. The Amsterdammers also signed Jofre Torrents from FC Barcelona.

Ajax signed the 19-year-old on an initial free transfer, although bonuses included in the deal mean Ajax may pay a few million euros to the Spanish giants. Torrents' contract with Ajax runs until June 2030.

Torrents is yet to make an appearance for Ajax. He has been on the bench for several games, but both Henrique and Wijndal seem to be ahead of him in the pecking order.

Wijndal started four of Ajax's games during UEFA Conference League qualifying, scoring against Shelbourne FC. He also started against Willem II in Ajax's 5-1 win over the club from Tilburg.

While Wijndal is obviously more experienced than Torrents, the fact that Ajax was prepared to let him leave in the summer means he probably does not have a long-term future in Amsterdam. Wijndal's contract at Ajax expires in June 2027, and it currently seems unlikely that Ajax will look to extend that deal, given the fact that they signed two left-backs in the summer and were also open to letting him leave.

Wijndal came seemingly very close to leaving Ajax at the end of the summer transfer window, but that transfer collapsed late on, and he ended up staying in Amsterdam.

Torrents only made four appearances for Barcelona before leaving. He is therefore still extremely inexperienced, but Henrique's absence provides Michel with the opportunity to give the Spaniard minutes, allowing him to gain match sharpness and adapt to first-team football.

articles.title: Starting XI: Proper Footy’s Back – Is This The Team We’ll Line Up With Today?
articles.summary: We’re predicting two changes to the team that played against Manchester City.
articles.body:
Man, that three week break seemed to take forever. It's ridiculous to have such a long break just as we're getting started, and predictably some players have picked up knocks which will rule them out for the foreseeable. Still, the break's given Le Bris some valuable time with a key core who didn't go away – Xhaka, Mukiele, Meunier, Le Fee and Reinildo – and that could be really important over the coming weeks. Today, we kick off what will be a testing couple of months, and here's how I think we'll line up against a Brighton team who've deservedly been praised for their excellent start to the season

While Roef's league stats look bad this season for the number of goals he's conceded versus shots saved, he's done ok – although he should have done better with two or three of Man City's goals last time out. Roefs has set high standards for himself, and will be looking to kickstart his season today with a solid display.

Defence: Nordi Mukiele, Kevin Danso, Omar Alderete, Dayann Methalie

Ballard's injury opens the door up for someone to come into the team – but who will it be. Feasibly, Hume or Meunier could play at right back and Nordi play centrally, however I do think we've missed the balance of the left footer on the left of the central pairing, so after proving his fitness during the international fixtures Alderete could come in to partner Kevin Danso at the back. While it's a shame Ballard has picked up his injury I don't think he looks convincing on the left hand side, and it's been interesting he's been asked to do that role, rather than Danso. I reckon Mukiele will keep his place at right back, while Dayann Methalie could keep his place at left back after an excellent Premier League debut at the Etihad last time out. The only curve ball there may be that Reinildo's been at the AOL for the last few weeks and Methalie's been off on internationals – but given the nature of the game today I think Methalie's attacking instincts could be valuable.

Midfield: Thomas Meunier, Enzo Le Fee, Granit Xhaka, Noah Sadiki, Nilson Angulo

The midfield central three picks itself – as long as the concerns over Sadiki's fitness don't amount to anything – so it's the wide positions that create some intrigue, as always. I think we'll go with Meunier on the right, and this will give us some tactical flexibility as he can either drop back a little to create a five – which would free Angulo up in this instance to join the attack, or cover Nordi when he attacks if we're in a four. Either way, I think it's nailed on he starts. On the left, Angulo's been impressive in the main this season and I can't see him sitting this one out – although with Fofana breathing down his neck he's got to keep up his performance levels.

It's such a shame Brobbey picked up an injury, particularly after having probably his best game for us against City. That said, it's a big opportunity for Wilson Isidor to really get stuck into the action, and he's fresh off some impressive performances for Haiti over the past few weeks.

articles.title: Tottenham news: Tottenham fly to Marbella for team-bonding camp
articles.summary: Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi to take his squad to Marbella for team-bonding training camp after clash against Manchester United
articles.body:
Tottenham will fly to Spain for a training camp following Saturday's Premier League game at Manchester United .

Roberto de Zerbi's side are bottom of the table following a winless start to the season, with two draws from five games.

With nine days between the game at Old Trafford and Monday's home game against newly promoted Coventry, De Zerbi hopes spending time in Marbella, southern Spain, can help kick-start their campaign and provide a chance for their new-look squad to bond.

Temperatures are predicted to reach 25 degrees in Marbella, while rain is forecast in Enfield, where Tottenham 's training base is located.

Such trips are unusual this early into the season, and certainly so soon after the international break, with English clubs usually searching warmer weather in winter.

Tottenham spent more than £250m on new talent over the summer - adding 10 players to their squad.

The busy fixture schedule and extended international break has meant that the new-look squad, with Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo, Mykhailo Mudryk and Omar Marmoush joining in the last week of the transfer window, has not had much opportunity to gel.

articles.title: Delight for Scotland's Erin Cuthbert in 2-0 Czech Republic win after long summer of recovery
articles.summary: Erin Cuthbert expresses joy and relief at making her first appearance of the season in Scotland's impressive 2-0 win over Czech Republic.
articles.body:
Erin Cuthbert expressed joy and relief at making her first appearance of the season in Scotland's impressive 2-0 win over the Czech Republic.

By winning the Women's World Cup round-one play-off away leg, the Scots are well set up for the return in Paisley on Tuesday, with Sweden the likely opponent for the team that progresses.

Chelsea captain Cuthbert, 28, is yet to feature at club level this season following a knee injury and came on as a substitute in Pardubice. Fellow sub Claire Emslie finished superbly for the Scots' second after captain Caroline Weir's stunning opener.

"It's so good," Cuthbert told BBC Scotland.

"It's been such a long summer. It's always great to come on and play for my country again - I'll never take it for granted when I get a serious injury.

"I'm just glad to get back on a football pitch. The relief, the amount of self-doubt that you have, the amount of stress - am I going to be back to the same level, how am I going to perform, is my knee going to be alright? All those things run through your head.

"It was a bad one. I was in crutches and a brace for the best part of a month. I lost a fair amount of muscle and over the summer I was trying to rebuild all of that again.

"It's been a really, really hard journey."

Emslie scored her first goal since becoming a mum, with her son and mother attending the game in Pardubice.

"I'm incredibly proud of her," Cuthbert said of Emslie. "I have an enormous amount of respect for her. Everything's just so impressive - to be a mum, to play at the highest level."

The Czech Republic were given a late reprieve when the award of a penalty was overturned but, soon after, Cuthbert was "flabbergasted" a late challenge on her in the box did not result in a spot-kick.

And while Cuthbert was "delighted" with the win, she cautioned that 2-0 can be a "dangerous" lead.

"We're a good team and when we play on the front foot, we can hurt teams," she added. "The best form of attack is defence."

articles.title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto to remain under police protection
articles.summary: Pinto’s lawyers recently denounced irregularities in the proceedings, highlighting the real threats facing their client.
articles.body:
Computer hacker Rui Pinto , the man behind the Football Leaks website that helped trigger the Premier League probe into Manchester City’s finances , will remain under police protection, Portuguese authorities confirmed.

Pinto obtained private documents that showed City broke league rules from 2009 to 2018. An independent commission found City guilty of all but one of 115 charges brought against them over breaches of Premier League financial rules.

His witness protection measures, which were due to end on Saturday, October 10, will now remain in effect pending a new decision, the Ministry of Justice said in a statement.

A previous resolution was nullified because Pinto had not been “duly informed of the reasons for the decision” and had not had the opportunity to challenge it, the statement added on Friday.

Pinto’s lawyers last week denounced irregularities in the proceedings, highlighting the real threats facing their client, who was assaulted in Lisbon last April.

The 37-year-old said he had to move to a secret location “due to the multiple death threats” he had received.

Pinto has been a protected witness since 2020 after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest.

Arrested in Hungary, where he was living in January 2019, and extradited to his home country, Portugal, Pinto spent more than a year in pre-trial detention before agreeing to cooperate with authorities by granting them access to the encrypted data in his possession.

Pinto was both a defendant and a protected witness in the Portuguese justice system. He is also cooperating with investigators from other European countries.

During his first trial, the former history student and self-taught computer expert admitted hacking computers to obtain millions of documents, which he began publishing online in late 2015.

Passed on to a consortium of European investigative media outlets, this wealth of information exposed questionable practices involving star football players, clubs and agents, subsequently leading to tax adjustments and judicial investigations in several countries.

A Portuguese court handed Pinto a suspended four-year sentence in September 2023 after he was found guilty on counts of attempted extortion, illegal access to data and breach of correspondence.
